source_title: New York International Antiquarian Book Fair
titles: Quadragesimale de Aeternis Fructibus Spiritus Sancti [Sermons 41 to 61] ([Quadragesimal Sermons, i.e. Sermons for Lent])
languages: Latin (Latin); Italian (a few notes in Italian)
places: Northern Italy, Italy, Europe (Northern Italy, Milan (?)); Milan, Lombardy, Northern Italy, Italy, Europe (Northern Italy, Milan (?))
other_info:
Amply annotated by contemporary hands and transcribed during the author’s lifetime, this collection of Quadragesimal sermons (24 of the 61 known sermons) is by the understudied Italian preacher Antonius da Vercelli (d. 1483) of the Observant Franciscan movement. His sermons boast a strong didactic and catechetical character; they are enhanced by
a plethora of exempla as well as plentiful quotes from scriptural, patristic, and lay authors. Known in only three manuscripts, only one of them complete, and unpublished, the collection merits a critical edition.

other_info: Although tiny and compact like many miscellanies used by the mendicant friars, this manuscript was an expensive production. It is copied in a formal script by well-trained scribes and includes an illuminated frontispiece at the beginning of the main text, the Confessionale of Bartholomaeus de Chaimis, an influential but rare text that still lacks a scholarly edition. Dated by the scribe, this is perhaps the oldest surviving copy and may have been produced under the direct super-vision of the author.

titles: Rubricated Breviary, Use of Rome, in Latin
places: San Giovanni in Conca, Milan, Lombardy, Northern Italy, Italy, Europe
manuscript_binding: 19th-c. Parisian binding signed by (Alphonse?) Similer. Very dark green leather over pasteboards; covers tooled in gilt with outer frame enclosing another frame, center of each cover with four-pointed motif; doublures of brown leather; edges gilt
other_info:
[See cat. for additional notes, description, and bibliography.] 144-5 x 99-102 mm (95-6 x 69-70 mm). iii (modern paper) + 484 + iii (modern paper). Pencil foliation ii-iii, 1-483 (marbled folios i and 484 not foliated). A previous modern pencil foliation on every tenth leaf was out of sequence after f. 330. 50 quires mostly of 10. Ruled in very faint grey or brown ink. Written in a "fere humanistica" bookhand, apparently by Dionisius de Castello, priest of S. Giovanni in Conca, Milan, throughout. | Contents. 1r-6v Ambrosian calendar, with an entry for almost every day of the year; each month headed by a verse on the unlucky days in brown ink. 7r-12v Roman calendar, with an entry for almost every day. 13r-192v Temporale. 193r-194v General Rubrics. 195r-v Table of scriptural readings for September. 195v-197r New Rubrics, in the order of the months. 197r-v Form of absolution from excommunication. 198v Rubric for feasts during the octave of Corpus Christi, here attr. Pope John XII. 199r blank. 199v-200r Hymn "Verbum caro factum est." 201r-277r Ferial Psalter. 277r-279r Litany. 279v Seven Penitential Psalms. 279v-280v Pater Noster, Ave Maria, Gloria in excelsis, Apostles' Creed, Nicene Creed, Invitatory Psalm (Ps. 94) in two slightly different versions. 281r-291v Hymnal for proper and common feasts. 292r Prayers "Aue regina celorum," "Domine sancte pater omnipotens eterne deus," "Omnipotens sempiterne deus." 292r-v Miscellaneous notes: calendrical rubrics on finding dates; verses on the properties of fennel (also in 14th-c. Avignon, Bibliotheque du Musee Calvet MS 606). 293-425r Sancorale. 425v-431r Extra offices and prayers: Office of the Transfiguration, Office of Saint Anne, three short prayers of St. Anastasia. 432r-458r Common of Saints. 458r-460r Order of Grace. 460r-465r Office of the Virgin, Use of Rome. 465r-468v Office of the Dead, Use of Rome. 468v-476v Ritual of the Last Sacraments. 477r-478v Forms for blessing: salt and water, an altar, incense, bread. 478v-480v Additional lections for the Common of Saints. 480v Date 1465 and scribal colophon. 480v-481r Contemporary additional comemorations, by two of three different hands, of St. Thomas Aquinas, Sts. Hermagoras and Fortunatus, and the Holy Cross. | Decoration. Five historiated initials, of varying size, depicting mostly half-length figures. Seven similar smaller painted foliate initials. 4-, 3-, 2-, 1-line initials. | Signed and dated by Dionisius de Castello at end of volume; date "1464" also at end of Hymnal. Unidentified near-contemporary Italian owner(s) added Hermagoras and Fortunatas to the second calendar and the additions at the end of the volume, suggesting a special veneration (principal patrons at Udine, Gorizia, and Laibach (Llubljana)). Unidentified French Collector, 19th-c., with small gilt red leather bookplate, not that of Charles X of France as previously proposed. Collection of Baron Francois-Florentin-Achille Seilliere sold Sotheby's 24 February 1887 and four following days, lot 180, bought by Ridler for £13; probably bought by Buchanan immediately afterwards.
